messages:
Tess: hey team :wave: day 2 on runtime onboarding. trying to build from source on Ubuntu 22.04 VM. installed CUDA 13.1 with the runfile but skipped the bundled driver. cmake/ninja fails linking with undefined refs to cuInit/cuDeviceGet. `ldd build/bin/runtime` shows `libcuda.so.1 => not found`. any quick troubleshooting tips?
Mika: welcome! :tada: can you paste `nvidia-smi` and the last ~10 lines of the linker error?
Tess: sure — nvidia-smi and the link tail:
```
$ nvidia-smi
Tue Mar  9 14:12:01 2026
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 535.113       Driver Version: 535.113       CUDA Version: 13.1     |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
```
/usr/bin/ld: build/liblibruntime.a(cuda_driver.o): in function `InitDriver':
cuda_driver.cpp:(.text+0x1a7): undefined reference to `cuInit'
cuda_driver.cpp:(.text+0x1d0): undefined reference to `cuDeviceGet'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```
Tess: and `ldd build/bin/runtime` output: `libcuda.so.1 => not found` but I do have `/usr/local/cuda-13/lib64/libcuda.so.1` from the runfile install.
Samir: that's the usual culprit — the real `libcuda` comes from the kernel driver package and should live in `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu`. If ldd can't find it, the dynamic loader path is missing it or the driver isn't installed. Did you install `nvidia-driver-535` from apt or skip it?
Tess: I skipped driver in the runfile because I thought apt had it.
Rosie: common gotcha. two options: (1) install the distro driver package (`sudo apt install nvidia-driver-535`) and run `sudo ldconfig`, or (2) add `/usr/local/cuda-13/lib64` to `/etc/ld.so.conf.d/cuda.conf` and `sudo ldconfig` as a short-term fix. prefer installing the driver package so kernel/driver match.
Tess: I ran `sudo apt install nvidia-driver-535` and `sudo ldconfig`. now `ldd build/bin/runtime` shows `libcuda.so.1 => /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1`. re-running the build now fails in the nvcc/ptx step: `ptxas: error: /usr/local/cuda-13/bin/ptxas: Illegal instruction`.
buildkite: [ci/runtime-build #128] failed after 12m — step "compile-kernels" exited 1. tail of build log: `ptxas: info : 64-bit ELF     : /usr/local/cuda-13/bin/ptxas
ptxas: error: Illegal instruction
make: *** [kernels] Error 1`
Mika: `Illegal instruction` usually means the ptxas binary you're running uses CPU instructions not supported by your VM host (e.g., AVX512). is this a small cloud VM with older cpu? `lscpu` output?
Tess: it's an older Skylake-based VM. `file /usr/local/cuda-13/bin/ptxas` shows ELF 64-bit but running it locally hits Illegal instruction.
Samir: yep — NV's distributed ptxas can be built with modern microarch flags. two practical routes: (A) build inside an NVIDIA-provided docker container that matches the toolkit (nvcr.io/nvidia/cuda:13.1-devel-ubuntu22.04) so ptxas is compatible with their userland, or (B) install the toolkit from the distro packages (apt) which tends to have compatible ptxas for older CPUs, or (C) use a newer VM with CPU features required.
Rosie: also avoid copying `libcuda` from one place to another — that causes weird ABI mismatches. if you go container route, bind-mount your source and use `--gpus` so the container talks to host driver. example:
```
docker run --gpus all --rm -it -v $PWD:/src -w /src nvcr.io/nvidia/cuda:13.1-devel-ubuntu22.04 bash
cmake -S . -B build && cmake --build build
```
Tess: tried the container approach — built inside the cuda:13.1-devel image and ptxas runs fine there. build completed. :white_check_mark: thanks!
Mika: great. for our onboarding notes: prefer distro driver package + either build in an NVIDIA container or use a host with required CPU flags to avoid ptxas issues. adding this to the eng-runtime onboarding doc would save others.
Samir: I'll add a short checklist to the wiki: verify `nvidia-smi`, ensure `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1` exists, prefer apt `nvidia-driver-535`, and if ptxas Illegal instruction occurs, use the official CUDA container or proper toolkit package.
Tess: thanks all — saved my afternoon. :clap:
